hypothesis: If physical conditions do not determine biotic similarity, then ecoregions sharing the same climate-defined biome (Mediterranean-type) in Australia, South Africa and Chile must lie in different biogeographic realms (distinct faunas and floras) rather than in one shared realm.
pass_criterion: Among ecoregions with BIOME_NUM = 12 (Mediterranean Forests, Woodlands and Scrub), the SW Australian ecoregions (e.g. Jarrah-Karri forest, Swan Coastal Plain, Mallee), the Cape ecoregions of South Africa (e.g. Renosterveld, Fynbos) and the central Chile ecoregion (Chilean Matorral) fall in three pairwise-different REALM values (expected Australasia, Afrotropic, Neotropic), AND the biome spans at least 4 distinct realms across all its ecoregions. Claim supported only if both conditions hold.
fail_criterion: Claim refuted if any two of the three regions (SW Australia, Cape of South Africa, central Chile) share the same REALM, or if BIOME_NUM 12 ecoregions span fewer than 3 realms, indicating that climate-defined biome predicts realm.
interpretation: Darwin's 'climatal and other physical conditions' are proxied by WWF biome (BIOME_NUM/BIOME_NAME), a classification based on climate and vegetation physiognomy; 'inhabitants/faunas and floras' are proxied by REALM, which delimits regions by shared evolutionary history and taxonomic composition. The 25-35 degrees S example is located via ECO_NAME and polygon centroids. Modern reinterpretation: biome is a vegetation-structure proxy for climate, not direct climate variables, and the test is a categorical contrast, not a variance partition; a fuller test would add climate rasters. Only the 'dissimilarity despite similar conditions' half of the claim is tested here; the 'similarity despite different conditions' half is not.

dataset.name: WWF Terrestrial Ecoregions of the World
dataset.publisher: World Wildlife Fund (WWF), distributed via Source Cooperative (cboettig/ecoregion)
dataset.why_it_fits: Open GeoParquet/geodatabase of 847 ecoregions with REALM, BIOME_NUM, BIOME_NAME and ECO_NAME fields plus polygon geometry; allows cross-tabulating climate-defined biome against biogeographic realm and locating the Australian, South African and Chilean Mediterranean-biome ecoregions. The README cites the related paper doi 10.1093/biosci/bix014, but that is the article, not a DOI for this dataset copy.
